title: Mole removal
what: A mole is removed with a scalpel, a laser, or a radio wave device, with local numbing. Most often, the tissue is sent to the lab to be checked.
why: If a mole changes, gets in the way, gets injured, or looks suspicious to a skin doctor.
tell_doctor: If you tend to get raised, thick scars, called keloids

prepare.title: Before removal
prepare.text: First, a skin doctor checks the mole with a special magnifier and decides how to remove it.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not tan for 2 weeks before and after. Do not put cream on the spot on the day of the procedure.

bring: Your referral or the skin doctor's report
steps: The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A numbing injection is given, and the area goes numb
The doctor removes the mole with a small margin of healthy skin
If there was a cut, a few stitches are put in
A dressing or plaster goes on top
The tissue is sent to the lab to be checked
feel: The numbing injection stings for a couple of seconds. After that, you only feel touch
after: Keep the area clean and dry as your doctor says
Stitches usually come out after 7 to 14 days
Lab results come in 1 to 2 weeks
Do not tan, and protect the area from the sun for a few months
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop when you press on it
Redness, swelling, pus, or fever. These are signs of infection

faq.a: If there is any doubt at all, a scalpel. It keeps the tissue whole for the lab. The doctor decides after the exam.
A small mark almost always remains. Over time, it usually fades.
